rows.grounds: fused form: tathā + eva + unmīlane + api; indicates the same holds in the open-eyed state
fused form: syāt + etat + dhyānasya; states the defining mark of that meditation

items.question: What characteristic mark defines that meditation even in the open-eyed state?
premises: The same condition applies even when the eyes are open.
That meditation has a recognizable defining mark.
The mark persists beyond closed-eye absorption.
items.inference: Therefore, the defining mark of that meditation remains present even in the state of outward opening.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'that meditation' depends on the immediately preceding verses.
items.plain_english: Even when the eyes are open, this would be the characteristic mark of that meditation.

rows.grounds: one whose own form is Brahman
the movements and operations of the whole world

items.question: What does one of Brahman-nature know about the activity of the universe?
premises: The knower is described as having the nature of supreme Brahman.
Such a knower cognizes the activity of the universe.
Knowledge here extends to the world's operations.
items.inference: Therefore, one established in Brahman-nature knows the supreme reality and the activity of the universe.
uncertainties: Whether 'vetti' implies discursive knowledge or direct recognition is not explicit.
items.plain_english: Being of the nature of supreme Brahman, such a one knows the activity of the whole universe.

rows.grounds: the state of being an attendant or servant
enter into or assume a state
together with the lords or rulers of mantras

items.question: What relationship do the mantras and their lords assume toward such a realized being?
premises: The mantras are said to enter a state of service.
The lords of mantras act together with the mantras.
This service is presented as a consequence of the realized state.
items.inference: Therefore, the mantras together with their lords become servants of that realized being.
uncertainties: The verse does not explicitly restate the subject to whom they become servants.
items.plain_english: Indeed, the mantras, together with the lords of mantras, enter into service.

rows.grounds: fused form: sanmantraḥ + tat + dhyānam; every utterance becomes true mantra and that meditation
fused form: yat + nirīkṣaṇam; any act of seeing or observation

items.question: How are ordinary speech and ordinary seeing transformed for one in this realized condition?
premises: Every instance of speech is included without exception.
Every instance of seeing is included without exception.
Speech becomes true mantra and meditation in this state.
items.inference: Therefore, for such a one, all speech becomes true mantra and meditation, and all seeing is likewise transformed.
uncertainties: The predicate for 'yannirīkṣaṇam' is compressed and must be understood from the parallel structure.
items.plain_english: Whatever speech there is becomes a true mantra and that meditation; whatever seeing there is is likewise transformed.

rows.grounds: distributive relative of place, repeated for emphasis
correlative demonstrative of place, repeated for emphasis

items.question: Where do states of absorption arise when the mind moves in this condition?
premises: The mind may go to any place or object.
Each place the mind reaches is included without exception.
Absorption arises in those very places.
items.inference: Therefore, wherever the mind goes, there absorption is present.
items.plain_english: Wherever the mind goes, there, in every such place, absorptions arise.

rows.grounds: repeated possessive, emphatic or transmitted as given
locative demonstrative referring to the supreme self

items.question: What happens to a person's karmas when the supreme Self is directly seen?
premises: The supreme Self can be directly seen.
Karmas are subject to exhaustion.
Seeing the supreme Self is presented as the condition for this exhaustion.
items.inference: Therefore, when the supreme Self is seen, that person's karmas are destroyed.
uncertainties: The repetition of 'asya' may be emphatic or a textual peculiarity.
items.plain_english: And when that supreme Self is seen, this person's karmas are destroyed.

rows.grounds: the status or realm of gods and demons
fused form: yat + tat + prāptam + ca + api; even that state which may be attained
rows.morph: pron.n.nom.sg + pron.n.nom.sg + n.nom.sg (past participle, √prāp) + indecl. + indecl.

rows.grounds: is taken up, accepted, or clung to

items.question: Why does attainment of divine or demonic status fail to attract the one who has seen the supreme Self?
premises: States such as those of gods or demons may be attained.
Such attainment is possible even for the realized one.
The realized one does not grasp or cling to that attainment.
items.inference: Therefore, even if divine or demonic status is attained, it is not grasped by such a one.
uncertainties: The subject is implied from the preceding verse rather than stated explicitly.
items.plain_english: Even if the state of gods or demons is attained, it is not grasped.

rows.grounds: fused form: kiñcit + anālabhyam; nothing remains unattainable
something that remains to be known
fused form: na + avaśiṣyate; does not remain over

items.question: What remains unattained or unknown for the one established in this realization?
premises: The realized person is the subject of the statement.
Nothing is described as unattainable for that person.
Nothing is described as remaining to be known.
items.inference: Therefore, for that realized one, nothing remains unattainable and nothing remains to be known.
items.plain_english: For that one, there is nothing unattainable and nothing left to be known.

rows.grounds: the abode or state of peace
the practice of focused holding or dhāraṇā

items.question: What need remains for yoga or concentration once the state of peace is attained?
premises: The state of peace has been attained.
Yoga is a means or discipline ordinarily employed.
Concentration is likewise a means or discipline ordinarily employed.
items.inference: Therefore, once the state of peace is attained, neither yoga nor concentration remains necessary.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, when the state of peace has been attained, there is no need for yoga and no need for concentration.

rows.grounds: an instrument used to create a breeze
locative absolute: when present or attained
the natural cool breeze from the Malaya mountains

items.question: What purpose does a palm-leaf fan serve when the Malaya breeze is already present?
premises: A palm-leaf fan is a means to produce a breeze.
The Malaya breeze is already present.
An inferior means is unnecessary when the desired condition is already given.
items.inference: Therefore, when the Malaya breeze is present, a palm-leaf fan serves no purpose.
items.plain_english: What use is a palm-leaf fan when the Malaya breeze is already blowing?

rows.grounds: fused form: na + asti; does not exist as a requirement
fused form: svayam + om + iti; seeing oneself as Om in this way
for those who perceive or recognize thus

items.question: Why are restraint and observance no longer operative for those who see themselves as Om?
premises: Yama and niyama are ordinarily prescribed disciplines.
Some perceive themselves as Om.
For such perceivers, these disciplines are said not to apply.
items.inference: Therefore, for those who see themselves as Om, restraint and observance are no longer required.
uncertainties: The exact force of 'svayamomiti' is compressed and interpretively rendered as self-recognition as Om.
items.plain_english: For those who see themselves as Om, there is no restraint and no observance.

rows.grounds: fused form: jīva-ātmanoḥ + āhuḥ + yogam; they call the oneness of jīva and ātman yoga
fused form: āhuḥ + yogam; repeated or transmitted as given

items.question: How do experts in yoga define yoga in terms of the individual self and the Self?
premises: Experts in yoga offer a definition of yoga.
The definition concerns the relation of jīva and ātman.
That relation is stated as oneness.
items.inference: Therefore, according to experts in yoga, yoga is the oneness of the individual self and the Self.
uncertainties: The repetition of 'āhuryogaṃ' appears redundant and may reflect transmission or emphasis.
items.plain_english: The experts in yoga say that yoga is the oneness of the individual self and the Self.
